items.title: Stage 1 — a Metal-first baseline that boots on arm64
items.verdict: First running arm64 build with Metal as the only configured renderer. Carried the fix for the `[3][31]`-array constructor overflow and moved decryption onto the ARMv8 AES extensions.
items.note: The overflow had been papered over by a `// HACK: ... garbage data` comment for years. Root-causing it deleted both the hack and the bug.

items.title: Delete the OpenGL and Vulkan backends
items.verdict: Metal is the only renderer. The GLSL emitter and glslang went with them.
items.note: Deleting a backend exposes coupling only the linker finds: the MSL emitter forward-declared four helpers that were **defined in the GLSL emitter's translation unit**, and several files were receiving `robin_hood` and `StringBuf` only transitively through Vulkan includes.

items.title: The documented one-`MAP_JIT`-region-per-process limit is not enforced
items.verdict: 4,000 regions succeed under hardened runtime on macOS 26. The risk this would have forced a custom JIT allocator is retired.
items.note: A first probe appeared to confirm the limit — it was testing an RWX pattern xbyak never uses. **Probe the pattern the code actually uses, not the one the docs describe.** Preserved in `tools/probes/`.

items.title: Remove the stale macOS "preview version" disclaimer
items.verdict: Upstream's warning that macOS is a preview is not true of a fork that targets only macOS. Also started ignoring `Roms/`.

items.title: Golden-scene capture harness
items.verdict: `testing/capture-scene.sh` records a window-only frame plus FPS/RSS/threads into `testing/golden/baseline.tsv`, which is the committed record every claim here is checked against.
items.note: There is no test suite in this repo. Verification is: it builds, it boots a title, the frame looks right, and nothing new appears in the log. The harness is what makes the last two checkable.

items.title: Delete the x86-64 recompiler backend and all x86 IML machinery
items.verdict: `BackendX64/` is gone. The `IMLUtil_*` helpers were kept as substrate for an AArch64 replacement.
items.note: The only backend peephole pass that existed was x86-specific and went with it — there is currently **no backend peephole pass at all**.

items.title: Rewrite `cpu_features` for arm64
items.verdict: The remaining x86 SIMD paths are gone. `g_CPUFeatures` now exposes `performanceCores` / `efficiencyCores`, which is what lets worker pools be sized against the right cluster.

items.title: Target macOS 26 / arm64 only; normalize the architecture macros
items.verdict: `precompiled.h` `#error`s on any other target. CMake hygiene alongside it: the inactive AppleClang warning fixed, and LTO left off in `RelWithDebInfo` deliberately.
items.note: LTO off keeps relinks fast and keeps `.o` files real Mach-O so `llvm-objdump` can inspect generated code. `Release` turns ThinLTO on and the objects become LLVM bitcode.

items.title: Fix 16 KB page handling in `MemMapper` and the MMU range table
items.verdict: Mapping rounded the base but not the length, and unmapping rounded nothing — so releasing a guest range failed silently with `EINVAL` and left it writable across a title switch.
items.note: Apple Silicon's 16 KB pages make this reachable where 4 KB pages hid it. A real bug the port surfaced rather than introduced.

items.title: Fix the JIT code-size and emitter-cursor bugs in the AArch64 backend
items.verdict: The cursor stopped short of the end of generated code, so `readyRE()` invalidated only part of the I-cache — a stale-instruction hazard that surfaces only on cold paths.
items.note: The follow-up corrected a docs claim that xbyak performs no I-cache maintenance. It does.

items.title: Sign the app bundle from CMake; split release and debug entitlements
items.verdict: Signing happens inner-out — nested dylibs first, bundle last — as part of the build rather than as a manual step.

items.title: Crash diagnostics: alternate signal stack, arm64 PC recovery, real backtraces
items.verdict: A stack-overflow SIGSEGV can now be reported instead of killing the handler, and backtraces are demangled with a recovered arm64 PC.

items.title: Instrument the JIT code leak instead of building reclamation for it
items.verdict: Epoch-based reclamation is a large piece of machinery for a leak nobody had measured. A counter went in first; reclamation waits on that counter showing a problem.

items.title: Stage 4 — `FSpinlock` becomes `os_unfair_lock`, then thread QoS
items.verdict: `SetThreadName(name, ThreadRole)` maps a role to a QoS class: guest cores and the GPU command thread `USER_INTERACTIVE`, compile and background work `UTILITY`. 16 call sites pass a role.
items.note: Order mattered. A raw spinlock plus QoS on asymmetric cores can hang; `os_unfair_lock` donates priority, so the lock change had to land first. `UTILITY` rather than `BACKGROUND` because macOS throttles the latter hard.

items.title: Audio: lock-free SPSC ring, and a latency request above the device floor
items.verdict: The mixer had been taking a mutex on CoreAudio's realtime thread — an unfixable priority inversion and a glitch source.
items.note: The fix is not QoS. Raising the audio thread's priority would have made the inversion worse, not better; the callback itself had to stop blocking.

items.title: Native macOS integration: screensaver, SDL event thread, Info.plist, no Carbon
items.verdict: Screensaver inhibition through `NSProcessInfo`; SDL input off a 5 ms main-thread timer onto its own thread; Carbon key codes dropped; `NSHighResolutionCapable` added.
items.note: Without `NSHighResolutionCapable` macOS ran the whole app magnified and handed Metal a **half-resolution drawable**. SDL's own screensaver path was disabled on macOS because it initialises `SDL_INIT_VIDEO` inside a wx app that already owns `NSApplication`.

items.title: Native `GameController.framework` input provider
items.verdict: A first-party input path that does not go through SDL.
items.note: `controllerProfiles/` ships empty, which is why input looks broken out of the box. Scripted driving writes a keyboard profile directly — the GUI combo boxes do not respond to accessibility scripting.

items.title: Three idle spins removed from the scheduler and command processor
items.verdict: **1.77× less total process CPU on Mario Kart 8 — 184% → 104% of one core — at an identical locked 60 FPS.**
items.note: An earlier baseline blamed `mach_continuous_time` at 47% self on the graphics idle path. Wrong caller: it was `__OSThreadCoreIdle` → `__OSCheckSystemEvents`, an unbounded busy-wait in the **scheduler**. Both idle-wait bugs were invisible to the `hostInstrCount / ppcInstrCount` metric the plan had ranked first — profile before picking a codegen target.

items.title: Apply sampler LOD bias, and stop graphic packs corrupting GPU registers
items.verdict: LOD bias was being computed and never applied. `MTLSamplerDescriptor.lodBias` is new in macOS 26.0, which a fork pinned to macOS 26 can simply use.

items.title: The TBDR work was rejected — then the rejection was found to be scene-dependent
items.verdict: The audit closed the whole TBDR workstream on the argument that the GPU was idle at 2.83 ms/frame. It had sampled the **MK8 title card**, not gameplay. On a real scene the GPU is at 87.7% of a 16.67 ms budget.
items.note: MK8's attract mode spends most of its wall-clock on the title card, so a short trace silently measures a near-idle scene. Gate on `draws/f > 200` to isolate race frames. The corrected verdict restored the graphics workstream and set the precondition — a GPU-heavy scene — under which the audit would later be redone.

items.title: Memoryless depth and load/store action audit
items.verdict: The safe wins are small and the large one needs pass-count work first. Later closed permanently for this scene: depth is **sampled by a shader on 390 draws/frame**, so `StoreActionDontCare` is not available.

items.title: The deferred texture copy is retired — the pass churn was buffer uploads
items.verdict: Built against the hypothesis that texture copies were breaking render passes. They were not; buffer uploads were. The mechanism was removed and the finding kept.
items.ref: 00-master-plan.md — The render-pass churn was buffer uploads

items.title: A code-anchored Wii U hardware reference — and two bugs it found
items.verdict: Ten documents in `docs/hardware/`, written against the emulator's own source rather than wiki lore. Writing them surfaced two real bugs.

items.title: The telemetry harness — counters compiled into the core
items.verdict: X-macro `.def` → enum → `__thread` TLS rows, cache-line striped and summed at the frame boundary. Proven free when disabled *before* anything was instrumented. Every performance claim on this page comes from it.
items.note: Phase 1 deliberately re-derived a result already known by other means, as a check on the instrument. Phase 3 found BotW was missing 31 imports. The follow-up fixed a race and a hot-path allocation the harness itself had introduced.
items.ref: 00-master-plan.md — Instrumenting three open questions at once

items.title: Decompose the frame: the open world is not GPU-bound, it is vsync-quantised
items.verdict: Korok Forest issues **fewer** draws than the shrine and leaves the GPU idle 62% of the time, yet runs slower. 49.90 ms is exactly three vsync slots, and p99 equals the median — no variance, which is the signature of quantisation, not of variable work.
items.note: **Re-measured at HEAD and confirmed**, n=3: 49.90 ms median, p99 49.98–50.00, 3,517–3,528 draws and 202–203 passes per frame. The original derivation predates the phase-split fix `491f4ef`, so it was re-run with the segmenting reporter rather than assumed to still hold.

items.title: CPU counters: nothing is saturated
items.verdict: All three guest cores together are busy 26.89 ms of a 49.90 ms frame — **18% of three-core capacity**. There is no CPU wall to knock down.
items.note: **Re-measured at HEAD and confirmed**, n=3: 26.84–27.18 ms across the three cores, 17.9–18.2% of capacity. This is the number that deprioritised the whole CPU workstream, and it was originally n=1 taken before the phase split, so it was the one most worth re-running.

items.title: 52,330 free HLE calls per frame, and where the context switches come from
items.verdict: Every HLE call advances guest time by **zero cycles**, including `FSReadFile`, which on hardware is an IPC round trip to IOSU. And **79.4% of the 3,143 thread switches per frame are the guest voluntarily calling `OSYieldThread`** — BotW polling, faithfully emulated, because Cafe OS scheduling is cooperative.
items.note: A flat per-call charge is ruled out by measurement, not opinion: `cpu.hle_would_charge_cycles` sums a hypothetical 500/call to **163% of the cycles actually retired**. The volume is `OSFastMutex_Lock/Unlock`, `OSGetCoreId` and GX2 register setters — tens of cycles each on hardware. Any charge must be tiered per function. **Re-measured at HEAD and confirmed**, n=3: 51,974–53,276 calls, 3,138–3,142 switches, the yield/quantum/blocked split 79.4–79.5% / 10.4–10.5% / 10.0%, and the charge ratio 163–164%. The blocked breakdown reproduces exactly: sleep 52%, message queue 24%, event 15%, semaphore 9%.

items.title: Park the GPU fence wait instead of spinning
items.verdict: One guest fence was being spun on **65 million times a second**. Parking it cut a further **20% of process CPU** in BotW with no frame-rate change.
items.note: No frame-rate change was the correct outcome and is now understood: the guest was never waiting for the GPU. See `cp-fence-vsync`.
items.ref: 00-master-plan.md — The menu waits on the fence exactly as long as the open world does

items.title: Rebrand to TesseraEmu, and migrate the user data directory in place
items.verdict: Existing installs migrate rather than losing their saves and settings. Verified from the new path that nothing depended on the old one.

items.title: CI on the fork, and the bugs it was hiding
items.verdict: Getting the build check green turned out to require fixing two real bugs it had been failing to report.

items.title: Recover the translation sources, and an Arabic catalog broken twice over
items.verdict: The `.pot` generation check was added, then immediately broke the Arabic plural forms; both the check and the catalog were fixed.
items.note: ~30 changed `_()` strings across 19 locales are still untranslated — see the roadmap.

items.title: The README, rewritten around the fork and corrected as the record moved
items.verdict: Describes what this fork is rather than what upstream is not, and states the goal (the best way to run Wii U games on a Mac) separately from the readiness (early, two titles, one machine, no releases).
items.note: Successive corrections were of numbers invalidated by the immediately preceding commits, then of a two-column table that scored upstream rather than describing this fork, then of a tone that overcorrected into calling the project a research curiosity. Three hand-typed numbers had gone stale by `584521b` — 107 counters against 115, 155 anchors against 163 — one of them contradicting a passage two sections below it explaining why such counts are not typed. The title of this entry used to carry a correction count, which was the same mistake in miniature.

items.title: Measure the fiber switch: 454 ns, a 70× gap, and not a frame-rate fix
items.verdict: `swapcontext` costs **454.5 ns** against **6.5 ns** for a hand-written AArch64 switch — `swapcontext` on Darwin/arm64 calls `sigprocmask` on both save and restore. At 3,143 switches/frame that is **1.43 ms/frame**, 2.9% of the frame.
items.note: Worth doing for power and headroom, not for fps: the frame already fits its work into one vsync period with 16.6% headroom, so removing 1.4 ms crosses no boundary. A microbenchmark is the right instrument — `Fiber::Switch` does not return until the fiber is resumed, so an in-process scope timer measures descheduled time and reported 197 ms of "busy" inside a 49.9 ms frame. (Status corrected 2026-08-03: this entry is the *measurement*, which landed; `rm-fiber-switch` carries the deferred rewrite. `deferred` in `items[]` violated this file's own schema.)

items.title: Instrument three open questions at once; two answers killed the work
items.verdict: `IT_MEM_SEMAPHORE` and the wait-for-flip spin are **exactly zero** in BotW. Snapshotting guest threads at fence-stall entry found the cores idle 95% of the time — against a 96% baseline, so it discriminated nothing.
items.note: A probe with no control sample cannot discriminate. The 95%-vs-96% result is the cleanest example of that on this fork.

items.title: A BotW run is two workloads, and blending them invented a result
items.verdict: `drive-botw.sh` spends its first ~4,050 frames in menus at 113 draws and 33.27 ms, then ~4,750 frames of gameplay at 3,516 draws and 49.90 ms. A whole-file median lands wherever the phase ratio falls and **describes no frame that occurred**.
items.note: This is not hypothetical. It produced a confident **"−6.2% GPU busy"** for a change whose real effect is +0.5%, because two runs of the same script had slightly different menu-to-gameplay ratios. `telemetry-report.py` now segments by draw load and analyses the longest phase. Any BotW number in this repo predating it is suspect.

items.title: `cp_fence` is the vsync timer — solved, and never a defect
items.verdict: The fence releases **10 µs** after a vsync signal (p99 30 µs), exactly one vsync and one flip per stall, and the duration is identical in a 113-draw menu and in 3,516-draw gameplay. That is frame pacing working.
items.note: **Do not try to recover this 15.58 ms.** It retroactively explains why parking the spin and committing work early both changed nothing — the guest was never waiting for the GPU. One flip per vsync also pins `swapInterval = 1`, so the grid is 16.68 ms and a 49.90 ms frame is the title taking three slots.
items.ref: 00-master-plan.md — `cp_fence` solved: it is the vsync timer

items.title: The GPU's dead air: 33 ms idle per 50 ms frame, in two blocks
items.verdict: The idle is not diffuse — it is two large contiguous gaps, which is what made the next commit's single-cause explanation findable.
items.note: **Re-measured at HEAD and confirmed**, n=3: `gpu.gap_count` 7, `gpu.gap_large` 2, 32.67–32.68 ms of gap per frame, identical to three decimal places across runs.
items.ref: 00-master-plan.md — `cp_idle` and the GPU's 33 ms of dead air

items.title: BotW is 20 fps instead of 30 because of one config default
items.verdict: `gpu.frame_critical_path_ns` is **35.25 ms** against a two-slot deadline of 33.27 ms, so the frame takes three slots. Turning off **`GX2DrawdoneSync`** drops it to 18.64 ms and the scene to **30.06 fps**, deterministic across n=3 / n=2.
items.note: The cost is `GX2DrawDone`'s `IT_HLE_SYNC_ASYNC_OPERATIONS` packet, which BotW emits twice per frame and whose handler force-finishes readbacks with bare `waitUntilCompleted()` on the Latte thread: **6.78 ms/frame, of which 6.75 ms is texture-readback force-finish**. **The default was not changed** — it is a documented accuracy tradeoff, and that is a product call.

items.title: The `MTLEvent` wrap was real, and fixing it corrects every `gpu.busy_ns` ever recorded
items.verdict: `EVENT_VALUE_WRAP` was 4096, so the signalled value went backwards every ~29 s and periodically disabled command-buffer serialisation. `gpu.busy_ns` sums per-buffer intervals, so overlapping buffers were **double-counted**.
items.note: **Do not compare `gpu.busy_ns` across this commit.** The same scene reads 16.8 ms properly serialised against 19.1–19.4 before. The inflation grows with run length — the first wrap is ~29 s in — so old figures are inconsistently wrong, not uniformly so. Frame time and critical path were unaffected. The same commit fixed an uninitialised read; both were confounds.

items.title: Give command buffers a timeline instead of a pointer identity
items.verdict: Identity by pointer is unsound when the allocator reuses addresses. A monotonic timeline makes the ordering questions answerable at all.

items.title: What BotW actually reads back: 21 KB of float arrays per frame
items.verdict: Small, GPU-computed float arrays the guest genuinely consumes — delivered by draining the pipeline. The readback is not spurious, which is why the drain cannot simply be removed.

items.title: Reconcile CLAUDE.md, the README and the porting plans with the code
items.verdict: **Fourteen stale or wrong claims corrected in one pass**, across five documents.
items.note: The direct motivation for this status page: fourteen hand-typed facts had drifted from the code at once, and nothing in the workflow would have caught them.

items.title: Pass-structure audit on the open world — the shrine verdict does not transfer
items.verdict: 202–203 render passes, **73–74 of them same-FBO splits (36%)**, 804 MB/frame of attachment traffic, and **390 depth-sampled draws** where the shrine had zero. **95.0–95.1% of the splits come from one call site**: `bufferCache_copyStreamoutToMainBuffer`.
items.note: The old TBDR verdict rested on "the GPU is idle" and explicitly invited revisit on a GPU-heavy title; Korok gameplay met that precondition. The earlier 1,749 MB/frame estimate was 2.2× high — the formats had never been confirmed.
items.ref: 00-master-plan.md — The rest of the G-list TBDR work is not worth doing

items.title: The GPU is ALU- and texture-bound, so the streamout work is cancelled
items.verdict: The premise was verified before the code was written, and it was false. **ALU and texture are the top limiter in 86.1% of active samples; the memory path in 12.8%.** Removing 300 MB/frame would relieve a subsystem that bottlenecks the GPU about an eighth of the time.
items.note: Per the plan's own gate: report and stop rather than build it anyway. The *other* gate passed and is recorded for whoever revisits — `gpu.streamout_read_fragment` is **0** against a vertex control of 1,136/frame, so a vertex-only intrapass barrier would be legal. The first version of that detector read zero on both counters because the scope was self-defeating; the control is the only reason it was caught rather than published.
items.ref: 00-master-plan.md — The GPU is ALU- and texture-bound

items.title: Three surfaces that lied about accurate barriers on Metal
items.verdict: A config default, a Debug menu checkbox and a startup log line all reported a setting **nothing reads**. `CheckIfRenderPassNeedsFlush`, its declaration and its call site have been inside `/* */` since `26e40a4` — it arrived already-commented in the upstream Metal PR and has never run.
items.note: The fork therefore runs permanently in the barriers-off regime: the speed is already banked in every number here, and the correctness cost is already being paid. The setting itself was kept, inert, so `settings.xml` round-trips and the self-dependency work has something to hang off.

items.title: This page, the rule that keeps it current, and its own upkeep
items.verdict: One generated page for what changed versus upstream, what was tried and what it measured. Commit list, diffstat, baseline rows and counter totals are read from the repo — only verdicts are hand-maintained. CI reports any commit that lands without a ledger entry.
items.note: It caught its own first bug: the counter parser read **114** against the real 113, matching the `TLM_COUNTER(...)` example inside the `.def`'s own header comment. Two self-references bound the design — a ledger entry cannot name the hash of the commit containing it, and the page embeds the commit that carries it — so CI advises rather than blocks, and `--check` is local-only. The tracker's own upkeep (claiming commits, stamping measurements, correcting the ledger) is claimed by this entry rather than excused under `unattributed`, so the act of tracking is itself tracked.

items.title: Re-measure the four oldest Korok verdicts at HEAD — all four hold
items.verdict: Twelve of sixteen measured entries were taken before one of the two commits that invalidate earlier numbers wholesale, so the four load-bearing ones were re-run at HEAD, n=3, default configuration. **Every claim reproduced**, most of them to the decimal: frame 49.90 ms, three-core busy 17.9–18.2%, 3,138–3,142 switches at a 79.4% yield share, `gap_count` 7 with `gap_large` 2.
items.note: The screen that selected them was mechanical — *does this entry predate `491f4ef` or `839466d`* — and mechanical screens over-select: a ratio like the yield share is insensitive to phase blending, and `839466d` only ever touched `gpu.busy_ns`. Re-running was still the cheap move, because one telemetry run refreshes all four at once and the alternative was arguing about which ones the gates really reached.
items.ref: 00-master-plan.md — Re-measuring the Korok verdicts at HEAD

items.title: A geometry-shader texture binding wrote past the end of the array
items.verdict: `MetalState::m_textures` held 54 slots but texture units are addressed as *stage base + unit* with the bases strided by 32 (PS 0, VS 32, **GS 64**), so it needed 82 — every geometry-shader binding wrote at 64–81, into `m_uniformBufferOffsets`. Neither the write nor the read path bounds-checked the unit.
items.note: Never observed because `gpu.draws_mesh` is **0** in the only scene anyone measures: a heavily instrumented fork carried a memory-corruption bug because the instrument was pointed elsewhere. There is nothing to measure and no run was possible, so the verification is a `static_assert` tying the array size to the stage bases — the same discipline `BackendAArch64.cpp` uses for its 14 field offsets. Also confirms the `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug` configuration compiles, which had never been tried in this fork.
items.ref: 00-master-plan.md — An audit with no game image

items.title: Wire the self-dependency counter — and find that item 3.1 is a different bug
items.verdict: `acc.render_self_dependency` had **no increment site anywhere**, so its zero meant nothing. Wiring it showed the gap is not "we never split": `LatteDecompilerAnalyzer.cpp:888-957` *does* detect the pixel case and `LatteDecompilerEmitMSL.cpp:2322-2328` rewrites it to a framebuffer fetch — **discarding the texture coordinate**, so a blur or offset tap silently reads self.
items.note: Detection only: no pass splitting, no behaviour change, guarded by `tlm::AreaEnabled`, sitting in the loop `BindStageResources` already runs beside the `gpu.depth_sampled_draws` hook that serves as its positive control. Three counters split covered (`acc.self_dep_fbfetch`) from uncovered (`acc.render_self_dependency`) from never-coverable (`acc.self_dep_nonpixel`), which is the answer this item needs. **It has never been run** — no game image is available — so every frequency claim about 3.1 remains a guess. It counts draws, not splits: `BindStageResources` executes after `GetRenderCommandEncoder()`, so a real fix must move the check ahead of that call.

items.title: What the accuracy register actually says about BotW: eight signals at zero
items.verdict: Every **wired** accuracy counter reads exactly zero across all 8,881 Korok frames — `d24_s8_use`, `unsupported_tex_format`, `unsupported_primitive`, `geometry_draw_dropped`, `draw_skipped_no_target`, `draw_skipped_shader_err`, `alpha_to_mask_draws`, `dcstorerange_no_notify`. The only non-zero is `acc.unsupported_hle_calls` at 44/frame.
items.note: Derived from runs already on disk, not newly measured. It retires a priority label: `acc.d24_s8_use` is the counter behind item 3.3's "live corruption path on every M-series Mac" — the path is real and the format table does disagree with the decoder, but **BotW never takes it**, so do not promote that item until some title reads non-zero. Two caveats carry equal weight: one title is not coverage, and **the evidence is untracked** — `testing/.gitignore` excludes `traces/`, so these runs exist on one machine and cannot currently be regenerated.
items.ref: 00-master-plan.md — An audit with no game image

items.title: Four corrections to the record, one of which would have written a bug
items.verdict: `CLAUDE.md` still said `MemMapperUnix.cpp` and the `MMURange` table "contain 4 KB assumptions" long after Stage 3 fixed both. `03-graphics-metal.md` told the next person to scan `m_state.m_textures` (a sticky global that is never cleared → spurious pass splits), called blend factors `0x0B`/`0x0C` constant-alpha when `LatteReg.h:778-779` names them `BLEND_BOTH_SRC_ALPHA`/`_INV_` and constant alpha is `0x13`/`0x14` already mapped, and asserted an `MTLBinaryArchive` payoff the code path disputes. A fifth correction (`968c724`): CLAUDE.md said the graphics ROM did not reproduce and all three `acc.self_dep_*` counters read zero. True before `97ae3ad` moved the detector, stale after it, and it was describing the fork's only graphics test as useless while that test was producing the measurement `rm-fbfetch-coordinate` rests on.
items.note: The blend-factor entry is the one that matters: it was written as a two-line fix and following it would have duplicated an existing mapping onto the wrong tokens. The `MTLBinaryArchive` paragraph is flagged for re-verification rather than deleted — the descriptor's functions come from `newLibrary(m_mslCode)`, so the archive may skip only the backend compile. Also noted there: cold-launch cost is **unmeasurable today**, because the shader-cache timer is inside `#if BOOST_OS_WINDOWS` and has never run on this fork's only platform.
items.ref: 00-master-plan.md — An audit with no game image

items.title: First CPU conformance result — and the recompiler is not the problem
items.verdict: `ppc750cl.s` — 23,502 lines of public-domain PowerPC assembly **validated by its author against real Espresso silicon** — now runs as Wii U homebrew. **1,030 failures, and the recompiler and interpreter arms are identical: zero unique to either.** 676 are FPSCR state bits the emulator does not maintain; **354 are wrong values**, of which only **3 are integer**.
items.note: The identical-arms result is the load-bearing one: whatever is wrong is in shared decode/semantics, not the AArch64 backend, which is the riskiest part of this fork and had never been conformance-tested. The FPSCR split was established by rebuilding with `IGNORE_FPSCR_STATE=1`, which the suite provides for implementations that skip that bookkeeping and which shifts no test address, so the two runs are directly comparable. Needs no game image, console, keys or SDK — which is why it was possible at all with `Roms/` empty. Failures are grouped by mnemonic in `report.py` (derived via objdump): **131 of the 354 are multiply-add/subtract forms**, which matches a documented Espresso deviation rather than a random distribution. CI gates the test infrastructure but deliberately does not run the ROM — see the strategy doc.

items.title: The self-dependency reproducer, and why it first read zero
items.verdict: A homebrew ROM that draws into a colour buffer while sampling that same surface, needing **no game image**. It reproduces: `acc.self_dep_fbfetch` reads **1.0/frame** while the other two read zero — exactly one of the covered/uncovered pair firing, which is the shape that says the detector works.
items.note: The first run read zero on all three, and the cause was placement rather than the test. `_initTextureBindingPointsMTL` (`LatteDecompilerAnalyzer.cpp:527`) skips assigning a binding point to any unit with `textureRenderTargetIndex != 255`, so a framebuffer-fetch unit is stripped from the resource mapping — `textureCount` was **0** — and both hooks sat inside a loop the covered case can never enter. `acc.self_dep_fbfetch` was unreachable code. It is now counted from `shader->textureRenderTargetIndex[]`, which survives into the shader object. **A counter reading zero can mean the hook is somewhere the case never reaches, which looks identical to the case not occurring.**

items.title: Audit the new test docs for reproducibility — and CLAUDE.md for accuracy
items.verdict: Two independent audits, judged strictly against the committed repo rather than against what the author remembered. The documentation audit found the graphics ROM had **no way to stop it and no way to read its result** — `telemetry-report.py` prints "non-zero only", and the entire published result is three zeros. The CLAUDE.md audit found ~20 inaccuracies including two wrong logging claims, two architecture claims that had drifted past their code, and one sentence that refuted itself.
items.note: The most useful finding was self-inflicted: the dead-counter trap bullet still listed `acc.render_self_dependency` after the same session wired it, so an agent trusting CLAUDE.md would have dismissed a real unresolved measurement as a missing hook. The recurring mechanism across three separate findings is **appending a correction without deleting what it corrects** — 'eight commits stale' (twenty), '20.04 fps is exactly 59.94/3' (which the same sentence then refutes), and the graphics negative retracted nine lines later. Worth watching for, since this file accumulates corrections by design.

items.title: The named-test ROM harness the plan actually specified
items.verdict: `testing/rom-tests/` — a growable suite of independently named assertions with per-test `.expected` files, a blacklist, and a two-arm config matrix. **17 assertions, all passing** across both recompiler and interpreter.
items.note: This step was previously marked done by redefining the deliverable: what existed was two suites each emitting one aggregate verdict, not the named-test harness with expectations and a blacklist that the plan specified. The distinction is that a named-test suite grows — a new test is a function and a table entry. Verified by injection: a regression exits 1, a missing expectation exits 1, a clean run exits 0, and the blacklist suppresses. One real hole was found and closed during that testing — iterating only over *actual* results means a ROM that crashes halfway reports a clean run, so expectations are now iterated too and a test emitting no verdict counts as `MISSING`.

items.title: Three defects on the graphic-pack output-shader path, one of them a crash
items.verdict: Installing any graphic pack carrying output.glsl aborted the process on the Latte thread (nil Metal vertex function, because all six GraphicPack2 construction sites passed GetOpenGlVertexSource regardless of renderer), and on the way there wrote a pipeline pointer ~1.9 KB past a 12-element array once per presented frame. A third defect on the same review, m_lastUsedFBO surviving rendertarget_deleteCachedFBO, was found by reading rather than running. All three are inherited and all three are still live upstream.
items.note: `acc.output_shader_custom` reads **1409 over 1409 frames** — once per present, which is what makes these continuous rather than one-shot. The guard written for the crash does not work: `RendererOutputShader`'s `if (!WaitForCompiled()) throw` never fires because `WaitForCompiled()` returns true on a failed Metal compile. With sRGB the out-of-bounds index wrapped in `uint8` to 5 instead of going out of bounds, aliasing the `s_hermit_shader_ud` slot in both directions — a wrong-pixels bug hiding behind a memory-safety one. Reproduced by `testing/graphics-tests/probe-pack`, which is kept as a fixture precisely because `titleIds=*` plus `default=1` makes it universal and self-enabling.

items.title: A pixel oracle for the self-dependency reproducer, and what it caught
items.verdict: The offset-texel case does not merely get rewritten to a framebuffer fetch, it reads the wrong pixel: 16 of 16 texels in the strip returned their own value instead of the neighbour's, with nothing in the `other` bucket. `rm-fbfetch-coordinate` now has a failing test instead of an inference.
items.note: `UINT_R32` so the compare is bit-exact with no filtering tolerance, which is piglit's `blending-in-shader` trick. The strip at `[0,16)` reads `[16,32)`, which it does not write, so no feedback race can explain the result away. Two controls: `selfdep_seed` caught the first run outright, where inherited render state left colour writes off and the whole surface read zero — without it, two real verdicts would have been misread as emulator bugs. `selfdep_caseA_same_texel` passes, which is what makes the Case B line trustworthy, since a real sample and a framebuffer fetch must agree on a fragment's own texel. `run.sh` warns when a control fails and deliberately does not gate on Case B, which is expected to fail until the fix lands.

items.title: Item 3.1 — split the render pass when a draw samples its own attachment
items.verdict: The uncovered self-dependency case now ends the encoder before joining a pass, and the result is verified in pixels, not inferred: `selfdep_caseC_vertex_stage` PASSES, with all 16 texels of the strip returning the seeded value after a vertex shader sampled the surface being rendered into. `acc.render_self_dependency` and `acc.self_dep_nonpixel` read non-zero for the first time in this fork's history.
items.note: The decisive detail is placement: the detector that has run since `97ae3ad` lives inside `BindStageResources`, where the encoder is already open and it can only count. `ShaderHasUncoveredSelfDependency` answers the same question *above* `GetRenderCommandEncoder()`, walking the shader's own resource-mapped units rather than the sticky global `m_state.m_textures`, per the correction already in the design doc. Units the framebuffer-fetch rewrite covered are skipped — never bound, so they cannot alias — which is why the common pixel case still costs nothing. `vk_accurate_barriers` was marked inert in `CemuConfig.h` and now does something for the first time. **Measured:** `acc.self_dep_pass_splits` 1, firing on exactly the one uncovered draw, against `acc.self_dep_fbfetch` 377 correctly not split. **Three defects in the first cut were found by adversarial review and fixed in `bad31b2`.** It scanned `m_activeFBO` while the pass actually open belongs to `m_lastUsedFBO`, and `GetRenderCommandEncoder`'s reuse tests are one-sided, so a *dropped* attachment stayed live in the encoder unseen — the MRT case this item most needs to catch. It did not mirror `BindStageResources`' dim-mismatch substitution, so it split for units resolving to a null texture. And the aliasing test is pointer identity on `LatteTexture*`, which is documented in place and filed as `rm-selfdep-alias-identity`. **Validated on a real title (2026-08-04, Korok Forest, equal-length arms).** `vkAccurateBarriers` on vs off: **15 splits/frame vs 0**, and everything else flat — 204 vs 203 passes/frame, 49.90 ms and 20.04 fps in both. The design doc's expectation that this item would *cost* frame rate is not borne out: 15 splits per frame add about one render pass and no measurable time. The scene reproduces the committed baseline (3516 draws/f against 3517–3528 on file), so it is the right scene and the arms differ only in the setting.

items.title: A shader stage with no Metal function aborted the process instead of dropping a draw
items.verdict: `MetalPipelineCompiler::Compile` passed a nil `GetFunction()` to `newRenderPipelineState`, which aborts from the Latte thread rather than returning an `NS::Error` — so the `if (error)` handler written for this could never run. It now checks the pointer, logs, counts `acc.pipeline_no_function` and skips the draw.
items.note: Third appearance of the same trap in one day: `IsCompiled()` here, `WaitForCompiled()` on the graphic-pack output-shader path (`92a9885`). Both report success for a shader whose MSL failed to compile. **The function pointer is the only signal that does not lie**, and that is now written down in CLAUDE.md. Found while building a vertex-stage self-dependency test, where one unsupported shader construct took the whole emulator down.

items.title: texelFetch outside the pixel stage emitted MSL referencing a parameter it never received
items.verdict: `LatteDecompilerAnalyzer.cpp:593` gated the `texUnitUsesTexelCoordinates -> hasUniformVarBlock` promotion on the pixel stage, while the `float2 tex{}Scale` SupportBuffer member and the `*supportBuffer.tex{}Scale` body reference are emitted for every stage and only the `constant SupportBuffer&` *parameter* is gated. A vertex or geometry shader using texel coordinates therefore produced MSL that failed with `use of undeclared identifier 'supportBuffer'`, yielding a nil function.
items.note: The first diagnosis, "vertex-stage texture sampling does not survive the MSL emitter", was **wrong and too broad** — vertex texture sampling works; the trigger is texel-coordinate access (`GPU7_TEX_INST_LD`, or a SAMPLE with all four coordinates unnormalized), and the sampler's element type is irrelevant. Verified by running three shader variants: `usampler2D`+`texelFetch` failed, `sampler2D`+`texelFetch` failed identically, `sampler2D`+`texture()` compiled. It stayed hidden because any other reason to set `hasUniformVarBlock` — streamout, point size, a disabled viewport scale, a remapped uniform mode — rescues the shader, so only a *minimal* non-pixel texelFetch trips it. Before `2bd3e06` this took the whole process down rather than dropping a draw.

items.title: The analyzer and the emitter disagreed about framebuffer-fetch coverage
items.verdict: `_initTextureBindingPointsMTL` stripped a covered unit's binding point unconditionally while the emitter's substitution was gated on the runtime option, so with `FramebufferFetch=false` every pixel-stage self-dependent draw emitted a sample against a unit with no binding, failed to compile and was refused. One predicate, `LatteMtl_IsUnitCoveredByFramebufferFetch`, now answers the question for all five sites.
items.note: Measured with the option off, before → after: `acc.pipeline_no_function` **4 → 0**, `acc.self_dep_fbfetch` **287 → 0** (it had been reporting coverage in the one arm where no rewrite happens), `acc.self_dep_pass_splits` and `acc.render_self_dependency` **1 → 250** as the pixel draws reach the uncovered path. Default arm unchanged. **Explicitly not fixed:** with the option off `selfdep_caseA_same_texel` still fails, now because the draw runs and samples 0 rather than because it vanished. Splitting resolves prior writes but the surface remains an attachment of the new pass, so sampling it stays undefined — a splitter cannot fix that, and `FramebufferFetch=true` remains strictly better and stays the default.

items.title: Self-dependency was blind to a second texture over the same guest memory
items.verdict: A draw sampling a different-format view of the surface it renders into was invisible to both halves of the mechanism — the analyzer compares format, the renderer compared `LatteTexture` pointers — while Cemu builds a second texture object for exactly that case (`LatteTexture.cpp:858` returns `VIEW_NOT_COMPATIBLE` on format alone). Matching `physAddress` as well catches it.
items.note: A/B on one ROM with one variable: pointer identity gives `render_self_dependency` 1 and `pass_splits` 1; adding the address match gives **2 and 2**. Conservative by choice — exact base-address equality, not range overlap, since over-splitting is this item's named risk; partial overlaps at different base addresses stay invisible and `list_dataOverlap` is the raw material if that ever matters. **The first Case D passed while testing nothing:** its shader multiplied the sampled value by `0.0`, so the fetch was optimised away, no texture was bound and no alias existed — yet the draw-ran assertion passed and the counter read 1, which is indistinguishable from the miss it was built to show. The ROM now logs `caseD_samplerVars` so a vanished sampler cannot be mistaken for a missed alias.

items.title: Self-dependency, sized on real content at last: 498 per frame, 99.7% of it covered
items.verdict: BotW Korok Forest runs **498 pixel-stage self-dependencies per frame**, of which all but one or two are covered by the decompiler's framebuffer-fetch rewrite. Six distinct shaders account for the uncovered remainder, every one of them pixel stage against a colour attachment.
items.note: This is the number every frequency claim about item 3.1 was previously guessing at. It also makes `rm-fbfetch-coordinate` far more consequential than it looked: the rewrite that discards the texture coordinate is applied **498 times a frame** in ordinary open-world play, and the reproducer proved it returns the wrong pixel for any offset tap. How many of the 498 are offset taps is the next question and is not answered here. Measured with the splitter enabled; the uncovered count is the same either way, since splitting changes what happens after detection, not what is detected.

items.title: The per-shader accurate-barrier override is not worth building
items.verdict: Its entire premise is that users turn accurate barriers off for performance, so known-problematic shaders must force them back on. Measured on Korok Forest, accurate barriers cost **nothing**: 49.90 ms and 20.04 fps with the splitter doing 15 splits/frame, identical to the arm with it disabled. If the setting is free there is no reason to disable it, and therefore nothing for an override to rescue.
items.note: **Correction to the first reading.** The lava base hash `6f6f6e7b9aae57af` IS present in Korok Forest. The earlier "appears zero times" was an artefact of instrumentation: that run carried no shader detail on the *covered* counter, so the hash had nothing to appear in. With the detail added it shows up immediately — in the **covered** set, handled by framebuffer fetch, not on the uncovered path an override would force a split for. The waterfall-foam hash `4c0bd596e3aef4a6` is still absent, and Korok has no waterfalls, so that one remains untested rather than refuted. None of this changes the cancellation, which rests on the cost being zero: if accurate barriers are free, nobody disables them, and an override has nothing to rescue.

items.title: Item 3.1 is shipped, and its headline warning was wrong
items.verdict: The pass splitter, the alias detection behind it and the `accurate_barriers` gate are all in. The remaining half of 3.1 — restricting the framebuffer-fetch substitution to cases where it is valid — is tracked separately as `rm-fbfetch-coordinate`, because it is a decompiler change rather than a scheduling one.
items.note: This entry stood open for months carrying the warning "expect it to **cost** frame rate — splitting passes raises pass count, the very thing the bandwidth work was trying to reduce." Measured on Korok Forest with equal-length arms: 15 splits/frame against 0, 204 passes/frame against 203, and 49.90 ms / 20.04 fps in **both**. The cost is not small, it is absent. It also predicted BotW lava and waterfalls as "the known cases"; the six shaders actually observed on the uncovered path are neither, though the scene contains neither hazard so that is untested rather than refuted. See `selfdep-pass-split`, `selfdep-alias-physaddr` and `self-dep-sized-on-botw`.

items.title: Every self-dependent sample in Korok Forest is a same-texel projective read
items.verdict: The 498 covered self-dependencies per frame resolve to **11 distinct shaders, 22 (shader, unit) pairs**, and every one samples at `varying.xy / varying.w` — a perspective divide of an interpolated clip-space position, i.e. the fragment's own screen position. **Not one adds an offset.** So the coordinate-discarding framebuffer-fetch substitution is valid for 100% of the self-dependencies in this scene, and `rm-fbfetch-coordinate` is a guard against future shaders rather than a fix for current wrong pixels.
items.note: Read from the emitted MSL, dumped with `FramebufferFetch=false` — with the substitution enabled the coordinate is already replaced by `col{N}` and the evidence is gone. The last write to the coordinate register before every sample is the multiply by the reciprocal, so "no offset" is a property of the code rather than of where I stopped looking. **Single scene.** Korok Forest has no waterfalls, no heat haze and no refraction, which are exactly the effects that would produce an offset tap; the waterfall-foam shader the design doc names never appears. This bounds the item for open-world play and says nothing about the rest of the game.

measured.scene: BotW Korok Forest, MSL dump with FramebufferFetch=false

items.title: FPSCR[RN] was never read, and implementing it fixed none of the 1030
items.verdict: Nothing in `src/Cafe/HW/Espresso/` read the guest's rounding mode: every conversion was a plain C++ cast or a host FP instruction, so the guest got round-to-nearest-even whatever FPSCR[RN] said. Now synced to the host FPU on `mtfsf`, `mtfsb1x` and guest-thread context load, which covers the recompiler too since both arms run guest FP on the host FPU. **The conformance count is unchanged at 1030.**
items.note: Kept because the divergence was real, not because it paid: a guest asking for round-toward-negative-infinity was silently given round-to-nearest. The suite only sets a non-default mode **3 times** in a whole run, verified by probe, which is why fixing it moves nothing. Two process errors worth recording. I read the `cemuLog_log` probe on stdout and saw zero hits, concluding the hook never fired — `LogType::Force` still needs `--verbose` to reach stdout, exactly as CLAUDE.md warns, and the hits were in log.txt all along. And I chased `frsp` as the top failure by reading the mnemonic table, which spans all 1030 records including the **676 FPSCR-state** failures that the roadmap gate explicitly says not to conflate with the 354 wrong values. The decoded `frsp` 'results' were not single-representable because they were not results.

items.title: ps_madd rounded the product before the add; its whole family did not
items.verdict: `PPCInterpreter_PS_MADD` wrapped the product in its own `(float)` cast before adding, so the intermediate was rounded to single twice. PowerPC multiply-add is fused: the product must not be rounded. Removing the inner cast takes the wrong-value count from **354 to 350** and `ps_madd` specifically from **16 to 12**.
items.note: Found by comparing against its own siblings: `PS_NMADD`, `PS_MSUB`, `PS_NMSUB` and `FMADDS` all cast only the whole expression, and `ps_madd` was the single member of the family that did not. The suite's own changelog names this case in as many words — *'fmadds/ps_madd is not rounded twice'*. **The full-suite count is unchanged at 1030**, because those four tests still fail their FPSCR-*state* check, which is the deliberate omission; only the values-only build shows the fix. That is also why the values-only build is the one to measure against.

refuted.title: The `MTLEvent` chain is what holds the frame back
refuted.verdict: `queue_latency_ns` (14.29 → 14.69 ms) and `command_buffers` (7 → 7) do not move between the 20 fps and 30 fps arms. Confirmed a second way by the wrap fix: buffers **had** been overlapping for most of every run, and it bought nothing.

refuted.title: The command-buffer commit threshold is mistuned
refuted.verdict: Same evidence as above — `command_buffers` is identical in both arms. Tuning when work is submitted cannot move a frame that is waiting on work already submitted.

refuted.title: The renderer is withholding work while the command processor blocks
refuted.verdict: True, and irrelevant. Work was held in **139,491 of 139,512** idle notifications per frame; committing at stall entry drops that **85%** and moves nothing else — frame time, fps, `cp_fence` and GPU busy all flat to within 0.6%.
refuted.note: The two notification sites look identical to the CP and are nothing alike: `RingStarvation` fires ~129,000×/frame inside a park-and-recheck loop, `FenceStall` once. Committing on the first would mint a command buffer per spin.

refuted.title: The readback drain can be made surgical
refuted.verdict: Measured three ways, all negative. `readback_forcestart` is 0, `readback_age_at_wait_ns` is 14.19 ms (the transfers had already been running ~7 ms each), and `readback_draws_ahead` is 169/frame against 3,516 draws — the blit is not stuck behind its own command buffer either.
refuted.ref: 00-master-plan.md — The readback drain is not surgically improvable

refuted.title: Exempting the readback command buffer from the event chain will help
refuted.verdict: n=3 per arm, **every performance range overlaps**: frame 49.90 both, critical path 35.13–35.22 vs 35.10–35.23, force-finish 6.21–6.34 vs 6.14–6.27. The only separated metric was `command_buffers` 7 → 9, which merely proves the arm was live.
refuted.note: Note the control-vs-control pair from that batch: `readback_forcefinish_ns` swings **±2% between identical runs** while frame time and critical path are stable to 0.0%. A "3% improvement" in that counter is noise.
refuted.ref: 00-master-plan.md — The readback drain is not surgically improvable

refuted.title: An in-pass streamout copy will recover the 1.90 ms
refuted.verdict: Cancelled by its own gate before being built. It would have removed 300 MB/frame of redundant tile traffic from a GPU that is bandwidth-limited **12.8%** of the time.
refuted.note: Unblocked only if the ALU bottleneck is ever addressed and bandwidth becomes the limiter. The legality question is already answered in its favour.
refuted.ref: 00-master-plan.md — The GPU is ALU- and texture-bound

refuted.title: `IT_MEM_SEMAPHORE` or the wait-for-flip spin is costing time
Snapshotting guest threads at fence-stall entry will show what blocks
refuted.verdict: Found the cores idle 95% of the time — against their 96% baseline idle rate. **A probe with no control sample cannot discriminate.**

refuted.title: The ring-buffer `wfe` park is saving CPU
refuted.verdict: It is a no-op. `sched_yield` is **36% of a core** in the same path.
refuted.ref: 00-master-plan.md — The ring-buffer `wfe` park is a no-op

refuted.title: Charging a flat cycle cost per HLE call will fix the timing divergence
refuted.verdict: A hypothetical 500 cycles/call sums to **25,103,500 against 15,384,240 actually retired — 163%.** It would more than double emulated guest time. Any charge must be tiered per function.

traps.title: A BotW telemetry run is two workloads, and the split is ~50/50
traps.body: ~4,050 frames of menu at 113 draws and 33.27 ms, then ~4,750 of gameplay at 3,516 draws and 49.90 ms. `--skip=60` removes none of it. A whole-file median describes no frame that occurred, and because two runs never have the same ratio, **that difference reads as a treatment effect**. It manufactured a confident −6.2%. Always pass `--phase=<gameplay>`.

traps.title: MK8's attract mode is not a fixed workload
traps.body: It cycles demo scenes with very different draw loads, so two traces taken minutes apart are not comparable and neither are their sample counts. A first A/B read as "4.4× faster" from sample counts; the real figure was 1.77×. To compare implementations, put a runtime toggle behind an env var, flip it every ~20 s **inside one process**, discard windows that straddle a switch, and report the median of n≥5 per variant.

traps.title: `xcprof compare` reports share of CPU, not absolute CPU
traps.body: If total CPU drops, everything that survives looks like a regression — it reported 15 of them for a change that cut CPU nearly in half. Use it to see *which* frames left the profile; use absolute process `cputime` over a fixed wall-clock window for the magnitude. Prefer `ps -o cputime=` deltas over `%cpu`, which is a decaying average.

traps.title: Do not divide BotW's GPU time by 16.67 ms
traps.body: BotW targets **30 FPS**, so the budget is 33.3 ms. An earlier revision divided by the 60 FPS budget and concluded the GPU was at "108–147% of budget" and "is what caps the frame rate" — both wrong. At ~50% duty cycle it is not the limiter in this scene, and cutting GPU time 16% moved the frame rate not at all.

traps.title: `cemuLog_log` does not write to stdout
traps.body: It writes to `~/Library/Application Support/TesseraEmu/log.txt`. Grepping the process's redirected stdout for errors — or for your own instrumentation — silently finds nothing and reads as "clean". Use `--verbose`. And `CemuApp::OnExit` calls `_Exit()`, so **`kill -9` loses buffered log and shader-cache writes**.

traps.title: Scripted edits fail silently
traps.body: Source uses tabs; a heredoc written with spaces will no-op a Python `str.replace` and report success. Worse, an anchor that is not unique attaches your counter to the wrong call site — that happened, and put a counter on the *temporary* render-pass path, reading 2–4 passes/frame instead of 202. It was caught by arithmetic, not by review. Prefer explicit line ranges and always `git diff --stat` before building.

traps.title: An in-process scope timer cannot measure a fiber switch
traps.body: `Fiber::Switch` does not return until the fiber is resumed, so the timer measures descheduled time. It reported **197 ms of "busy" inside a 49.9 ms frame**. A microbenchmark is the right instrument.

traps.title: A pixel diff of the MK8 title screen proves nothing
traps.body: The "Press A to start" prompt pulses and the background animates, so **~22% of pixels differ between any two captures**. Use targeted instrumentation to show a rendering change is live. Relatedly, `capture-scene.sh` uses `screencapture -R`, which grabs a screen *region* — raise the window first or you capture whatever is on top of it.

traps.title: GPU-time counters soak: the same frame costs 5% more GPU after four minutes
traps.body: Across the Korok gameplay phase, sliced into sixths, **draws (3,472→3,518), render passes (202), attachment bytes (800 MB) and CPU core-busy (9.4–9.5 ms) are all flat, while `gpu.busy_ns` climbs 16.9→17.8 ms and `gpu.readback_forcefinish_ns` climbs 6.5→7.5 ms** — identical work, more GPU time, reproduced in all three runs. So the *median* of those counters is a function of how long you recorded and where in the run you sampled, and two arms of an A/B must be equal-length and equally-positioned or the longer one loses. Frame time, fps and `frame_critical_path_ns` do not drift at all (0.0%) because they are vsync-pinned, which is why this hides. It also explains the recorded 16.45 ms against today's 17.12–17.15, and retroactively explains the "±2% swing between identical runs" noted for the drain counter — that was not noise, it was window placement.

traps.title: The build hash in every telemetry header is captured at cmake *configure* time
traps.body: `CMakeLists.txt:15` runs `git log --format=%h -1` inside `execute_process` and bakes the result into `-DEMULATOR_HASH`, which only re-evaluates when cmake reconfigures. A binary built from `cebe17f` reported `build 064d9a7` — eight commits stale — in its window title and in the `build` field of every `--telemetry` run header. `testing/capture-scene.sh` has the mirror-image problem: it stamps `baseline.tsv` with the *repo's* `git rev-parse HEAD`, which says nothing about what the binary was built from. **Neither surface proves provenance**; run `cmake -S . -B build …` before a measurement that will be quoted. The hash reaches everything through `precompiled.h`, so refreshing it costs a full rebuild.

traps.title: A counter reading zero is not evidence until you check it has an increment site
traps.body: Sweeping all 113 `TLM_COUNTER` declarations against `src/` found **14 that nothing ever writes**: `gpu.pipelines_compiled`, `acc.render_self_dependency`, and **all twelve `mem.*`**. The `mem.*` block covers buffer-cache scans and uploads, texture-cache reloads and shader-cache hit/miss — precisely the subsystem behind the largest graphics finding on file, that `UploadToBufferCache` fires ~25/frame and breaks render passes. That finding had to be established by backtrace attribution at every pass teardown **because these counters do not work**. The instrumentation for the question was sitting in the file reading zero, and zero was indistinguishable from "not wired". Check the hook exists, and prefer a positive control in the same code path — `gpu.depth_sampled_draws` reads 392/frame beside the self-dependency detector for exactly this reason.

traps.title: The instrument only sees the scene you point it at
traps.body: A confirmed out-of-bounds write — geometry-shader texture bindings landing past the end of `MetalState::m_textures` and into the next member — survived in a fork this heavily measured because `gpu.draws_mesh` is **0** in BotW Korok, the only scene anyone measures. Absence of a signal in the benchmark is not absence of the bug, and a scene chosen for being *exactly repeatable* is by construction a narrow one. Where a defect is structural rather than statistical, prove it with a `static_assert` and stop waiting for a run to show it.

traps.title: An update and DLC in mlc01 do not make a title bootable
traps.body: `~/Library/Application Support/TesseraEmu/mlc01/usr/title/` held `0005000e/101c9400` (BotW update, 3.0 GB, containing `U-King.rpx`) and `0005000c/101c9400` (DLC, 2.0 GB) — 5 GB of convincing-looking content with an executable in it. The **base** title is `00050000/…` and lives in `Roms/` as a disc image; an update carries only changed files, so with `Roms/` emptied nothing boots. Worth checking before planning any work whose verification is a run: the presence of `U-King.rpx` is not the presence of a game.

traps.title: A toolchain can be blocked two independent ways at once
traps.body: Building Wii U homebrew here needed devkitPPC, and the two obvious routes were both closed: the installer needs `sudo`, which cannot be answered when driving this repo remotely (and the agent shell has no TTY, so sudo's credential cache cannot carry across either), while `downloads.devkitpro.org` returns **403 via Cloudflare** — including its root, though `github.com` and `cloudflare.com` return 200, so it is site-specific. Critically that host serves **every** source devkitPro's buildscripts fetch, binutils/gcc/newlib included, not just their own components. The way through was that their download loop skips files that already exist and honours `BUILD_DKPRO_SRCDIR`, so pre-staging all six archives from GNU/sourceware/GitHub made the stock scripts work. Two genuine bugs in those scripts surfaced on the way: a three-argument call to a four-argument function in the mn10200 step, and no `--with-system-zlib`, whose bundled zlib defines `fdopen` to `NULL` and breaks the macOS SDK's `stdio.h`. All recorded in `docs/testing/00-test-strategy.md` §4.

traps.title: A homebrew sample reading zero frames is usually its own asset path, not the emulator
traps.body: wut's `gx2_triangle` booted cleanly, issued two command buffers and rendered **zero frames**, which reads exactly like a renderer defect. It is not. The sample loads its shader from the **SD card** — `WHBGetSdCardMountPath()`, backed by `<userdata>/sdcard/` — and **not** from the `.wuhb` bundle's `/vol/content`, so `WHBReadWholeFile` returned NULL and it `goto exit`ed before the render loop. Two compounding reasons it stayed invisible: the sample reports the failure through `WHBLogUdpInit` (**UDP**, port 4405) rather than OSReport, so `--forward-console-logging` showed nothing at all; and a title that exits early looks identical to one that renders nothing. `wut-tools` ships `udplogserver` to receive that stream. **Check a sample's own I/O and logging transport before suspecting the renderer**, and prefer `WHBLogCafeInit` in ROMs we write so the standard flag works.

traps.title: The graphics-test toolchain is three separate installs, and two of them are optional-looking but are not
traps.body: Building a Wii U test ROM needs devkitPPC (compiler), **wut-tools** (host utilities: `elf2rpl`, `rplimportgen`, `wuhbtool`) and **wut** (the library) — three separate builds. Missing wut-tools fails deep inside wut's build with `rplimportgen: No such file or directory` rather than anything resembling "a tool is missing". `wuhbtool` additionally needs **libfreeimage**, whose absence fails at *configure* time with `'libfreeimage' not found` and takes the whole tools build with it. And graphics tests additionally need **CafeGLSL**'s `glslcompiler.rpl` in `cafeLibs/` — without it a ROM builds fine and reports `glslcompiler.rpl-not-found` at runtime. `testing/toolchain/build-devkitppc.sh` does all of it; `testing/toolchain/README.md` explains why each piece is there.

roadmap.title: Shader cost — the ALU and texture work in the MSL the Latte decompiler emits
roadmap.verdict: Where the counters now point, and the only remaining frame-rate lever in this scene. Ordering- and bandwidth-shaped work is closed by measurement.
roadmap.gate: None — the measurement that closes every other avenue is what opens this one. But it is a materially different project from anything attempted so far and should be scoped rather than started from momentum.

roadmap.title: `MTLBinaryArchive` — stop recompiling every shader on every launch
roadmap.verdict: The persistent cache stores pipeline **state descriptors**, not compiled binaries, and replays them on the loading screen. The `MTLBinaryArchive` code that would fix this exists in `MetalPipelineCompiler.cpp` and is entirely commented out.
roadmap.gate: None. Highest-value item in the graphics plan after the correctness backlog; affects launch time rather than steady-state frame rate.

roadmap.title: In-pass streamout copy (revive)
roadmap.verdict: Would remove ~70 same-FBO pass splits and 300 MB/frame. The legality question is already settled in its favour — `gpu.streamout_read_fragment` is 0, so a vertex-only intrapass barrier is legal on Apple silicon.
roadmap.gate: **The ALU bottleneck must be addressed first** and bandwidth must become the limiter. Today it relieves a subsystem that bottlenecks the GPU 12.8% of the time.
roadmap.ref: 00-master-plan.md — The GPU is ALU- and texture-bound

roadmap.title: Batch streamout copies to a pass boundary (fallback)
roadmap.verdict: Turns ~70 splits into ~1 per boundary without needing any intrapass barrier. Needs a dirty-pending-copy bit forcing a flush on first read.
roadmap.gate: Same gate as the in-pass copy, and moot while the GPU is ALU-bound.

roadmap.title: Hand-written AArch64 fiber switch
roadmap.verdict: Measured at 70× — 454.5 ns → 6.5 ns, worth 1.43 ms/frame at 3,143 switches. Real, and not a frame-rate fix.
roadmap.gate: Do it for power and headroom, not for fps: the work in a frame already fits one vsync period with 16.6% headroom, so removing 1.4 ms crosses no boundary.

roadmap.title: Tiered per-function HLE cycle charge
roadmap.verdict: An accuracy gap, not a speed one: guest threads issue a million library calls a second at zero emulated cost, including calls that on hardware are IPC round trips to IOSU.
roadmap.gate: A flat charge is **ruled out by measurement** — it would inflate guest time to 163%. The histogram shows the volume is cheap primitives and the expensive calls are rare, so the tiering must be per function.

roadmap.title: AArch64 backend peephole pass
roadmap.verdict: There is currently none — the only one that existed was x86-specific and was deleted with the backend. The `IMLUtil_*` helpers were kept as substrate for a replacement.
roadmap.gate: Profile before picking a codegen target. Both idle-wait bugs found in Stage 5 were invisible to the instruction-count metric the plan had ranked first.

roadmap.title: Offset-0 addressing-mode fold
roadmap.verdict: Named in the CPU plan as the highest instruction-count win available.
roadmap.gate: Same as above — the CPU is 18% busy in the scene that limits us, so this buys headroom, not frames.

roadmap.title: Cycle counting as a first-class IML register
roadmap.verdict: The largest single win in the CPU plan for loop-heavy code.
roadmap.gate: Wants the differential correctness harness (02, item 0.3) in place first.

roadmap.title: FMA — a correctness fix that also removes instructions
roadmap.verdict: Strictly more correct than the current lowering, and cheaper. The trap is the PPC↔ARM mnemonic crossover.
roadmap.gate: Gated on the differential correctness harness (02, item 0.3).

roadmap.title: Epoch-based JIT code reclamation
roadmap.verdict: Deliberately not built. The leak was instrumented instead, and reclamation waits on that counter showing a problem.
roadmap.gate: The leak counter has to demonstrate a problem worth this much machinery.

roadmap.title: Reconcile the two contradictory Shrine measurement sets
roadmap.verdict: Two instruments disagree: 28.6 fps / 149 passes / ~1190 draws / 15.6 ms GPU versus 30.06 fps / 132 passes / 3784 draws / 14.0 ms. Different counting (draw *calls* vs draw *sequences*), and the GPU figures predate the `839466d` `busy_ns` fix.
roadmap.gate: None — one run with the current harness settles it. Until then, quote neither.

roadmap.title: Notarization and stapling in CI
roadmap.verdict: Signing from CMake is done; notarization is not. Needed before the DMG is distributable to anyone who did not build it.
roadmap.gate: None technical — needs credentials in CI.

roadmap.title: Housekeeping: 13 unincremented counters and 19 stale locales
roadmap.verdict: **Thirteen** counters are declared and never incremented: `gpu.pipelines_compiled` and all twelve `mem.*` (the twelfth, `mem.bufcache.upload_bytes`, is mentioned only in a doc comment). `acc.render_self_dependency` was the fourteenth and is now wired at `MetalRenderer.cpp:2434`. ~30 changed `_()` strings are untranslated across 19 locales.
roadmap.gate: None. Small, unglamorous, and neither blocks anything — but the `mem.*` block is not merely cosmetic: it is the instrumentation for buffer-cache and texture-cache behaviour, and its silence already cost one investigation.

roadmap.title: Restrict the framebuffer-fetch substitution to cases where it is valid
roadmap.verdict: **Confirmed by measurement.** The emitter rewrites every pixel-stage self-dependency to a coordinate-free framebuffer fetch — including the offset-sampling case, where it silently returns the current fragment instead of the neighbour. The reproducer alternates same-texel and offset-texel draws and both report as covered.
roadmap.gate: Still ungated and still has a failing test (`selfdep_caseB_offset_texel`), but **the urgency is now measured and it is low for open-world play**: all 22 self-dependent (shader, unit) pairs in Korok Forest are same-texel projective reads, so the substitution is valid for every one of them (`fbfetch-coordinate-sized`). Do it as a correctness guard, not as a fix for visible breakage. Before spending real effort, dump MSL from a scene that *would* break — a waterfall, heat haze, or water refraction — since a single scene cannot clear the whole game.

roadmap.title: The readback drain is 96% six tiny surfaces — ask whether they need mirroring
roadmap.verdict: 44 surfaces are mirrored per run; the **top 6 carry 96.2%** (96.1/96.2 in the other two runs). All are `TM_LINEAR_ALIGNED`, non-depth, ≤512 texels. The 6.9 ms/frame drain that costs this scene 30 fps is paid to mirror ~1.5 KB, 1.45×/frame.
roadmap.gate: Does **not** reopen `r-surgical-readback`: that refuted *reordering* the drain, and stays refuted. This is a policy question at `LatteTexture.cpp:1311`, where `enableReadback` is set for any linear-aligned surface on the theory the CPU might read it. The open question — does the guest ever read those six addresses — needs instrumentation and therefore a bootable title.
roadmap.ref: 00-master-plan.md — An audit with no game image

roadmap.title: Fix the 354 real floating-point and paired-single conformance failures
roadmap.verdict: 175 paired-single, 120 double-extended, 36 single-extended, 19 `psq_*`, 3 integer. These are wrong *values*, not wrong status bits, and they are shared between the interpreter and the recompiler.
roadmap.gate: None. **Measure against the values-only build, not the default one**: `make clean && make EXTRA_DEFSYM=-Wa,--defsym,IGNORE_FPSCR_STATE=1` gives exactly the 354 wrong values and makes `report.py`'s ranking meaningful. The default build's table is dominated by the 676 FPSCR-state failures and points at the wrong instructions — it ranks `frsp` first, which is a state failure. Real ranking of the 354: ps_nmadd 18, psq_st 16, ps_nmsub 16, frsp 15, ps_cmpo1 14, ps_mul 14, fctiw 13, with **131 in the multiply-add family**. `ps_madd` is fixed (`ps-madd-double-rounding`); its siblings have the correct fused *shape* already, so their cause is different and is the next thing to isolate.

roadmap.title: Every homebrew title that exits normally SIGSEGVs the emulator
roadmap.verdict: When the *guest* requests exit, `MainWindow::OnRequestGameExit` → `Close()` → `wxTopLevelWindowMac::Destroy()` → `wxWindow::Show(false)` faults in `objc_msgSend` on an `NSView`. Reproducible on every `.rpx` run, and the CLI branch it happens in is explicitly commented as existing *"for homebrew testing setups that use Cemu via CLI"*.
roadmap.gate: None. It does not corrupt results — the crash is strictly after the ROM's last output — but it makes the exit code useless, which blocks using a plain process exit status as a CI gate. **Two hypotheses already refuted, do not retry them:** (1) that the canvas was destroyed while the Latte thread was still presenting — adding `CafeSystem::ShutdownTitle()` + `DestroyCanvas()` before `Close()` changed nothing; (2) that closing from inside a dispatched event was the problem — deferring via `CallAfter` changed nothing. The identical backtrace in both cases points inside wx's own top-level teardown, not at our shutdown ordering.

roadmap.title: GetVerticesPerPrimitive returns 0 for six topologies the renderer accepts
roadmap.verdict: GetMtlPrimitiveType translates TRIANGLE_STRIP, TRIANGLE_FAN, QUADS, QUAD_STRIP, LINE_LOOP and LINE_STRIP_ADJACENT without complaint; GetVerticesPerPrimitive knows none of them. The mesh path used the result as a divisor, and AArch64 udiv by zero does not trap, so a geometry-shader draw at any of those topologies dispatched nothing. 92a9885 guards the divide and counts it; it does not supply the missing counts, because the correct value for a strip or a fan is a claim about the geometry-shader emulation that should be tested, not guessed.
roadmap.gate: A homebrew ROM that runs a geometry shader at strip/fan/quad topology. `acc.mesh_draw_no_vtx_count` and `gpu.draws_mesh` both read 0 in the probe ROM, which uses no geometry shader — unexercised, not absent. Until such a ROM exists there is no oracle for what the counts should be.

roadmap.title: GetCurrentCommandBufferId names a buffer that does not exist yet
roadmap.verdict: `m_submittedCount` is incremented inside CommitCommandBuffer, so calling GetCurrentCommandBufferId after a commit returns the id of the next, not-yet-recorded buffer. LatteQueryObjectMtl::end stores that, and getResult then reports 'not ready' while the samples are in fact ready. Upstream returned the buffer pointer, which stays valid after commit. This one is ours, introduced with the software timeline in 323e93f.
roadmap.gate: A ROM issuing GX2 occlusion queries. There is no such test today and BotW reportedly issues none, so the defect has no observable consequence in any scene currently measured — which is exactly why it survived review. Not worth changing the timeline design without a test that fails first.

roadmap.title: Verify and take upstream PR #1844's ASan/UBSan fixes
roadmap.verdict: Reported to carry three fixes we lack: two uninitialised pointers in MetalPipelineCache.h, an unordered_map::operator[] default-insert whose nulls are later release()d, and triangle fans drawn as MTLPrimitiveTypeTriangleStrip with the wrong topology. The fan/strip item is independently corroborated in our tree at LatteToMtl.cpp. Open upstream since 2026-03-21 and unmerged.
roadmap.gate: Read the diff. This is relayed from a subagent and was **not** verified against the PR by hand, unlike everything else filed today. Verify before acting, and treat the three-fix count as unconfirmed.

roadmap.title: Community graphic packs with GLSL output shaders cannot work on a Metal-only build
roadmap.verdict: On Metal, RendererOutputShader passes the pack's fragment source through verbatim, so output.glsl must contain MSL despite its name. 92a9885 stops that crashing, but a real GLSL pack from the community still cannot run: nothing translates it. Inherited behaviour, shared with upstream's Metal backend.
roadmap.gate: Decide whether this fork intends to support community output-shader packs at all. If yes it needs a GLSL-to-MSL path for output shaders specifically, which is a different and much smaller problem than the deleted Latte GLSL emitter. If no, it should fail with a legible message naming the pack rather than compiling nothing.

roadmap.title: Two fixes where we are ahead of upstream and could contribute back
roadmap.verdict: The MetalState::m_textures sizing bug (54 entries for indices reaching 81, so geometry-shader bindings wrote into m_uniformBufferOffsets) is still live at upstream's tip, as is the graphic-pack sampler override writing through into LatteGPUState.contextNew.SQ_TEX_SAMPLER. Both are small, portable and reviewable by reading. The three defects in gp-output-shader-path are upstream's too.
roadmap.gate: Upstream's contribution policy asks that submitted code be written and understood by a human, and this fork's changes were written with AI assistance. Anything sent must be re-derived and written by a person. That is a real cost and the reason this is deferred rather than open — see the note in README.md.

stages.title: Bootstrap and de-risk
stages.goal: Get a Metal-only arm64 build running at all, and retire the risks that would have invalidated the plan — chiefly whether MAP_JIT's documented one-region limit breaks the recompiler.

stages.title: The purge
stages.goal: Delete the alternatives rather than #ifdef around them: BackendX64, the x86 IML machinery, OpenGL, Vulkan/MoltenVK, glslang and the GLSL emitter.

stages.title: Correctness foundations
stages.goal: Fix what silently corrupts before optimising anything: 16 KB pages, the JIT cursor truncating I-cache flushes, signing, and arm64 crash diagnostics.

stages.title: Scheduling and native integration
stages.goal: Core counts before QoS, os_unfair_lock before priority donation, then native macOS integration.

stages.title: Performance, measured
stages.goal: Build the measurement harness first; nothing is claimable without it. Then follow the counters rather than intuition.

stages.title: Correctness and verification
stages.goal: Establish what the emulator actually gets wrong, with tests rather than opinion. Opened by the CPU conformance suite.
